entry.title: Tide Machine
entry.content: A lighthouse keeper's slot machine on a stormy night: pay the sea each tide, buy charms from a gull. Play it. New: reels.

entry.title: SPROUT·256: the future, as 1995 drew it
entry.content: The console now has a third tier: Eight.start({ bits: 256 }) gives a 480 by 270 screen in true colour where everything bright glows, with faint scanlines, sprites that turn and zoom, and four buttons in an arc, as on the big arcade machines. Smoky purple plastic over its circuits, a holographic sticker and a boot screen with a jingle. Starlane 2025 is its first game: surf a glowing lane into the sunset, boosting, jumping, spinning and bombing with all four buttons.

entry.title: HyperTalk in Sprout
entry.content: Text now has HyperTalk's chunks: "the quick brown fox" word 2 is quick, and t line 3 word 1, t item 2 and t char 1 read the same way. And stack makes an app a HyperCard stack: go next or by name, find words on any card, put a value into a field.

entry.title: A slightly soggy guide
entry.content: Sprout has a storybook now: the guide's first chapter teaches cells, records, collect and a tappable game, with two seedlings and a grumpy watering can. Every answer on the page was worked out by Sprout itself.

entry.title: A blog for Sprout
entry.content: From now on every change to Sprout gets a post here, a few lines long, and a feed. Posts are small files in sprout3/blog/, so builders working side by side each write their own.

entry.title: SPROUT·16
entry.content: Eight.start({ bits: 16 }) turns the console 16-bit: a 320 by 224 screen, 512 colours, and a warmer lead with a little echo. A game moves up by changing one number.

entry.title: Games made side by side
entry.content: A new game now lives in files of its own (games.d, tests8, skins), so seven games could be built at once without two hands on one file. node publish.js <game> puts one on the site in one go.

entry.title: Keys that repeat
entry.content: Hold an arrow and g input repeated "left" fires at once, again a quarter second in, then twelve times a second, the way a falling piece slides. Fizz Jar and Brick Snap play better for it.

entry.title: Games see a key go down
entry.content: The frame now hands every game pressed and released beside held: g input pressed "one" is true on the one tick a button goes in. No game has to remember last tick's keys any more.

entry.title: Lily and Chester
entry.content: A week at the stable with Lily and her horse Chester, then the county show. Play it. New: needs, for pet and farm games.

entry.title: Kits: library code that draws
entry.content: A kit is a Sprout module that draws with a game's own words, loaded when the game names it. The first, ui, holds what our games kept rewriting: ui banner, ui talk, ui meter, ui choices, ui wipe. Its examples state what they draw, and that is checked. See the library.

entry.title: Headstrong
entry.content: The first SPROUT·16 game: a big head with tiny arms and feet hops through a bathroom. Play it. New: platform, the feel of a platform hero in one step.

entry.title: Fizz Jar
entry.content: Pairs of fizzy drops fall on grumpy sours; four of a colour pop. Play it. New in the library: runs, for falling-block and matching games.

entry.title: Brick Snap
entry.content: Snap toy bricks onto an 8 by 8 baseplate and pop full rows and columns. Play it. New: piece, for block puzzles.

entry.title: Blade Beach '90
entry.content: Rollerblades, a boardwalk at sunset, a roller-derby giant. Play it. New: parallax, and a second kit, retro, that draws striped suns, palms and neon.

entry.title: Basketball Legends 8
entry.content: One on one against a legend of each decade, 1960 to forever, on an arcade cabinet. Play it. New: arc, for things thrown through the air.
